name: NRF on AI in Retail: Governance, Store Tools and Adoption
title: NRF on AI in Retail: Governance, Store Tools and Adoption
answer: The National Retail Federation's site covers how retailers are adopting AI, from customer-facing shopping assistants and agentic commerce to a formal governance framework. Its most useful single item is the NRF Center for Digital Risk & Innovation framework report setting out four principles for retail AI use, covering governance, customer trust, workforce oversight and business partner accountability.

sections.body: This is the website of the National Retail Federation, the US retail trade body, as read across sixty pages in October 2026. The material is a mix of blog posts, podcast pages for its Retail Gets Real series, press releases and event coverage, spanning NRF 2024 through NRF 2026. It is published by NRF itself and reports on its own research, summits and Innovation Lab exhibitors, alongside interviews with retailers, vendors and policy figures.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The site's central editorial thread is that AI has moved from experiment to core retail strategy. NRF's Center for Digital Risk & Innovation published a framework report, Principles for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Sector, described as the first articulation of core AI principles for retail, organised into governance and risk management, customer engagement and trust, workforce applications and use, and business partner accountability. Podcast coverage features PwC and Stripe discussing agentic AI, with consumers starting shopping journeys in AI agents and expecting to complete transactions inside conversational interfaces. Vendor stories describe Quin, a shopping assistant answering product, nutrition and returns questions in store, and Lily AI enriching product descriptions for Macy's, Bloomingdale's, J.Crew and Tapestry. NRF also reports on AI discrimination law, its founding membership of PACT AI, and Innovation Lab exhibitors including PSYKHE AI and Zenlytic.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: IDC ranks retail second among all sectors globally for AI spending, per NRF. NRF states retail contributes $5.3 trillion to annual GDP and supports 55 million working Americans. PSYKHE AI partners report a five-times revenue increase, three-times basket value, 26 percent higher retention and 4 percent lower returns. Lily AI sees 5 to 25 percent lifts in clicks, impressions and conversions. Zenlytic users report 20 hours a week saved at Koio and 31 percent year-on-year growth in a new category. The Retail Law Summit drew over 1,600 attendees.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in retail gets both the adoption picture and the rules around it. The framework report gives a citable governance position from the sector's main trade body, while the vendor and podcast coverage shows where spending and deployment are actually going, from in-store assistants to product discovery and conversational analytics. The legal coverage adds the compliance dimension that retail AI teams must track.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: The material is NRF's own output, so vendor results are reported as claims rather than independently verified, and several pages promote NRF events and membership. Coverage is US-centric and concentrated on NRF conference cycles, and the framework report is described as a starting point rather than a finished standard.
